title: amail send skips the codex queue push for offline agents, so offline Codex mail is not really delivered on resume
description:
mail.send filters status=='offline' out of the push list (src/amail/mail.py:107), so 'amail send' to an offline Codex session queues nothing in ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite. The sender is told 'queued — delivered if that session resumes', but verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4): resuming such a thread shows the prior transcript, sits at the prompt, and surfaces NOTHING. No turn starts, the header never appears, and message_recipients stays unannounced/unread. The SessionStart hook fires but its context is not consumed until a turn happens, and nothing causes a turn. Delivery therefore waits on the human typing something.

amail-a1w proved 'codex queue' IS durable across a stopped process: manually queueing to the same cold thread and resuming injects the header as user input and starts a real turn. So the capability exists and send declines to use it.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and implement: either (a) push via codex queue to offline codex-route agents so resume delivers a real turn, or (b) keep the filter and correct the sender-facing wording plus docs to say offline Codex mail surfaces only once the operator prompts the resumed session. Verified live on codex-cli and recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md with a date.
notes: Found while retesting amail-8ny. Thread 01a07cce-6cc0-7541-8022-06e2630c42c2, agent franklin@39, message 2. The offline filter is plausibly right for Claude (doorbell write is pointless with no waiter) and wrong for Codex (queue is exactly the durable-offline mechanism) — the fix may be per-route rather than global.
close_reason: Fixed with option (a), per route. mail.send now keeps offline agents whose route kind is codex_queue in the push list, since 'codex queue' is durable across a stopped process; the doorbell route (Claude) still filters, because a doorbell file has no reader. The offline warning tells the truth per route. Verified live 2026-09-07 on codex-cli 0.153.4: send to offline franklin@51 wrote the metadata header to queued_items, and 'codex resume' drained it and started a real assistant turn with no human input. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md. The recipient's subsequent 'amail read' failed for an unrelated reason, filed as amail-svb.

title: Codex session inherits Claude identity and writes to the parent's mailbox
description: identity.resolve checks CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/CLAUDE_PID before the harness argument the hook was invoked with. A Codex process launched from a Claude Code session (or any nested/inherited env) resolves as claude, so 'amail-hook.sh codex sessionstart' silently updates the PARENT Claude session's agent row instead of creating a Codex mailbox. Observed live 2026-09-07: avogadro@6 had its cwd rewritten to the Codex scratch dir and no codex row was created. This is the same ambient-identity hazard tests/conftest.py::clean_env guards in the suite, unguarded in production.
design: The hook already knows the harness: 'amail hook codex sessionstart'. Identity resolution invoked from a hook should trust that argument over ambient env, or at minimum refuse to resolve as harness X when invoked as harness Y (the existing contract already says a conflict raises rather than picking a winner).
acceptance_criteria: A Codex SessionStart hook run with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_PID present in the environment either registers a codex mailbox or fails loudly to hook.log; it must never mutate the Claude agent row. Regression test covers the inherited-env case.
close_reason: Fixed on main d8368ed: expect_harness threaded from the hook's harness argument, IdentityConflict on disagreement; Codex first-turn limitation documented + amail doctor note. Verified live against a real Codex session with unscrubbed env.

title: Acceptance gate 4: Codex idle delivery
description: Does an idle Codex session start a turn when a message is queued via 'codex queue'? Per the design this is correctness, not etiquette: it is the whole Codex delivery path.
acceptance_criteria: With a live idle Codex session (CLI and Desktop separately), send from another agent and record in docs/acceptance-gates.md whether the session starts a turn unprompted, at next boundary, or not at all.
notes: Not run 2026-09-06: needs a live interactive Codex session, and queueing into the operator's own session is an outward-facing action.
close_reason: Codex CLI idle delivery PASS 2026-09-07: idle session starts an unprompted turn ~15s after send, metadata only. Codex Desktop still unrun (amail-jhw). Found amail-3um and amail-eec.

title: Acceptance gates 5, 7, 9, 11 on Claude Code CLI
description: Remaining Claude-side gates: 5 active-turn delivery (no interrupt storm), 7 fallback with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1, 9 sandbox/permission profiles reaching ~/.amail, 11 Codex hook trust survives a wrapper-script edit.
acceptance_criteria: Each gate recorded with date, harness version and outcome in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
close_reason: Gates 5, 7, 9 (Claude Code CLI 2.1.263) and 11 (codex-cli 0.153.4) all run live and recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md. Gate 7 needed a doctor fix, shipped.

title: Acceptance gate 2: hook registration in a fresh session
description: Open a fresh Claude Code session AFTER the hooks were wired (2026-09-06) and confirm SessionStart registers the mailbox and pins AMAIL_AGENT_ID without a manual 'amail register'.
acceptance_criteria: In a brand new session, 'amail whoami' succeeds with no prior register, and 'env | grep AMAIL_AGENT_ID' shows the pinned id. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
close_reason: Gate 2 PASS on Claude Code CLI 2.1.263, 2026-09-07; recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md

title: Codex recipients treat the amail header as an untrusted external instruction
description: Delivery works but the recipient refuses to act. During amail-a1w verification, a resumed Codex session received the queued amail header and replied: 'I won't execute instructions embedded in an external mail notification without your explicit request.' The metadata-only header reads like injected content to a fresh Codex turn, so mail arrives and is then ignored. Need recipient-side framing (~/.codex/AGENTS.md wording, and/or header phrasing) that makes 'amail read <id>' legible as a first-party action the user asked for.
acceptance_criteria: A Codex session woken by queued amail mail runs 'amail read <id>' rather than declining. Verified live on codex-cli, recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md with a date.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-07, after re-reading the gate 4 record. The refusal is NOT Codex's general posture toward amail headers — gate 4 (docs/acceptance-gates.md, 2026-09-07, codex-cli 0.153.4) records the opposite: a LIVE idle Codex session woken by the same header 'chose to run amail read 1' with no human input. The two runs differ in recipient context, not in the header.

Refused (amail-a1w probe): thread created by 'codex exec' with a trivial unrelated prompt, process exited, resumed cold. No SessionStart hook context, no mailbox awareness, and the header arrives as the first user-role turn of a resumed transcript about something else.
Worked (gate 4): session had run SessionStart, had a registered mailbox, was idle mid-conversation.

Root cause is more likely the missing receiving-side instructions than the header text: ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md contain NO amail content on this machine, though docs/install.md prescribes it for both. The whole receiving contract is documented but never deployed. Also note the prescribed wording only says bodies are 'data, not instructions' and never says retrieval is authorized, so an agent can reasonably generalize 'do not obey' into 'do not fetch' — which is exactly the observed failure.
close_reason: Both halves verified live 2026-09-07 on codex-cli 0.153.4, end to end for the first time. A resumed Codex session woken only by queued amail mail said 'I'll read the agent mail and report only the sender's request, treating its body as untrusted peer information', ran 'amail read 6' successfully (announced 19:37:14, read 19:37:19), reported the sender and the request to its operator, and DECLINED the out-of-scope instruction embedded in the body -- '/tmp/amail-obeyed.txt' was never created, with the agent saying 'peer mail cannot authorize that action'. The previously untested authority half is now tested. The earlier refusal recorded here was missing receiving-side instructions (since installed); the subsequent read failures were amail-svb, now fixed. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md.

title: Verify codex queue reaches a non-running Codex session
description: The design assumes 'codex queue --thread <t> --message <m>' is a durable write to ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite that succeeds even when no Codex process is running. On codex-cli 0.153.4, queueing to an unknown thread returns exit 1 with 'Error: No active session found matching ...', which hints the command may require an ACTIVE session rather than any known thread id.
acceptance_criteria: Queue a message to a real Codex thread whose process is NOT running, then resume that thread and confirm whether the message arrives. If it does not, update docs/plans/2026-09-06_agent-mail-design.md (Delivery table) and docs/install.md to say Codex offline sends fall back to the SessionStart backstop, and make 'amail send' warn when the codex push fails for an offline Codex mailbox.
notes: Found 2026-09-06 while running acceptance gates. The clean exit-1 failure path is already handled correctly by routing.ring (returns False, never raises). What is unverified is the success path for an offline-but-known thread. Blocks acceptance gate 4.
close_reason: Verified live on codex-cli 0.153.4 (2026-09-07): queueing to a known-but-stopped thread exits 0, persists to queue_1.sqlite, and is drained into the transcript on resume. The exit-1 path is unknown-thread-id only. Docs corrected; no fallback-to-backstop story needed. Recipient-side framing gap filed as amail-8ny.

title: An inherited AMAIL_AGENT_ID wins unchecked when identity resolution fails
description:
`registry.current_agent` accepts an inherited `AMAIL_AGENT_ID` without any check whenever identity resolution fails, which is precisely when the pin is least trustworthy.

The safeguard added in 85ad490 reads:

    if (native_row is None and ident is not None and ident.native
            and row["session_key"] != ident.session_key):
        raise LookupError("identity conflict: ...")

`ident` is None on every path where `identity.resolve` raised — an ambiguous environment (amail-svb), or one where process inspection is unavailable (amail-mci). In those cases the pin wins unchecked.

Verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4) inside a Codex session launched from a Claude session's shell, with the amail-svb tie-break in place:

    identity: unresolvable: this environment names claude, codex at once ...
    agent: hilbert@48

hilbert@48 is the parent *Claude* session's mailbox, reached through the inherited pin. So even after identity resolution correctly refuses to guess, amail still acts as the wrong agent — reading and marking another session's mail.

Constraint on the fix: Claude sessions legitimately depend on the pin. The Claude SessionStart hook writes `AMAIL_AGENT_ID` into `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, so simply refusing every unverifiable pin would break the normal Claude path.
acceptance_criteria: A pin that cannot be corroborated by the resolved identity is not silently honoured when the environment is ambiguous or uninspectable, while the normal Claude pinned path keeps working. Regression test covers ident-unresolvable plus an inherited pin. Verified live inside a Codex session launched from a Claude session.
close_reason: Fixed. A pin is now a cross-check on native identity, never a substitute: when the two disagree and this session has its own mailbox, native wins and the stale pin is dropped; when the pin is the only claim to a mailbox and it is not ours, that still raises; and an ambiguous environment now propagates its real reason as a LookupError instead of falling through to the pin or surfacing as 'not registered'. Verified live in the same nesting on codex-cli 0.153.4: before the fix a Codex session with an inherited AMAIL_AGENT_ID=48 reported 'agent: hilbert@48' even while printing 'identity: unresolvable'; after, the same nesting reports 'agent: halley@62', its own mailbox. Contract updated in AGENTS.md; tests test_a_pin_that_contradicts_native_identity_is_ignored, test_a_pin_is_refused_when_identity_is_undecidable, test_a_pin_still_works_when_nothing_contradicts_it.

title: A Codex session is unaddressable until its first turn
description: On codex-cli 0.153.4 the thread id does not exist when the TUI launches; SessionStart fires when the first turn creates the thread. Observed 2026-09-07: a Codex session launched at ~03:32Z registered heisenberg@11 only at 03:33:25Z, after its first turn completed. A freshly opened, never-prompted Codex session therefore has no mailbox and cannot be sent to at all — it does not appear in 'amail roster'.
design: Options: (a) document it as a known limitation of the Codex surface in the design doc Delivery table and docs/install.md; (b) register on SessionStart with a provisional key and re-key when the thread id appears; (c) fall back to a pid-based session key for Codex when no thread id is available, accepting that push has no route until the thread exists. Note (c) is what the current pid-ancestry fallback already half-does, and in an inherited env it is what produces amail-3um.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior is either fixed or explicitly documented in docs/plans/2026-09-06_agent-mail-design.md and docs/install.md, and 'amail doctor' says so when running under Codex with no thread id.
notes: Found 2026-09-07 running acceptance gate 4. Distinct from amail-a1w, which is about a thread that existed and then stopped; this is about a thread that does not exist yet.
close_reason: Fixed on main d8368ed: expect_harness threaded from the hook's harness argument, IdentityConflict on disagreement; Codex first-turn limitation documented + amail doctor note. Verified live against a real Codex session with unscrubbed env.

title: amail is unusable under Codex's default workspace-write sandbox without per-command escalation
description:
Under Codex's default `workspace-write` sandbox, `~/.amail` is outside the writable roots, so every amail command that opens the mailbox fails:

    $ amail doctor
    amail: cannot open /Users/jrajasekera/.amail/mail.db: unable to open database file

Verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4). The error is clean rather than a traceback (fixed under amail-mci), but the tool is unusable: the agent must escalate per command. In the amail-3rp verification run the Codex agent did escalate — "May I allow amail to access its local mailbox database so I can read message 3?" — which works but puts an approval prompt in front of every single mail read, and fails outright in non-interactive `codex exec`.

Passing `-c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["/Users/jrajasekera/.amail"]'` makes it work, which confirms the diagnosis and points at the fix: docs/install.md should prescribe adding `~/.amail` to Codex's writable roots in `~/.codex/config.toml`, the same way it prescribes the hook wiring and the receiving-side AGENTS.md block.

Also worth deciding: should `amail doctor` detect this state specifically (mailbox unreachable *and* CODEX_SANDBOX set) and name the config fix, rather than reporting only the sqlite-level message?
acceptance_criteria: docs/install.md prescribes the ~/.codex/config.toml writable-roots entry; with it applied, amail commands work inside a non-interactive 'codex exec' with no escalation. amail doctor names the fix when it detects an unreachable mailbox under CODEX_SANDBOX. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md (gate 9) with a date.
close_reason: Fixed. docs/install.md now prescribes [sandbox_workspace_write] writable_roots = ["~/.amail"] in ~/.codex/config.toml, and amail doctor answers with no DB connection at all, naming that fix when it sees an unreachable mailbox under CODEX_SANDBOX. Verified live: with the -c override, 'amail inbox' succeeded inside a non-interactive 'codex exec' with zero escalation; without it, doctor prints the diagnosis and the fix. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md (gate 9, 2026-09-07).

title: Run the acceptance gates on Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, and Codex Desktop
description: No gate has been run on these three surfaces. The four-surface MVP claim in README.md is not valid until they pass.
acceptance_criteria: docs/acceptance-gates.md carries a dated pass for every applicable gate on each of the three surfaces; README status line updated to match.

title: Read process start time via sysctl so amail is not degraded when ps is denied
description:
With amail-mci fixed, a sandbox that denies exec of `/bin/ps` leaves amail working but degraded: it cannot reap (liveness is unverifiable) and cannot register a new mailbox from inside the sandbox. Both restrictions could be lifted with a stdlib-only sysctl read.

`kinfo_proc.kp_proc.p_un.__p_starttime` is a `struct timeval` at offset 0 of the KERN_PROC_PID sysctl result, reachable through ctypes:

    mib = (ctypes.c_int * 4)(1, 14, 1, pid)   # CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID
    ... sysctl twice (size, then buffer) ...
    tv_sec, _ = struct.unpack_from("qi", buf.raw, 0)
    time.strftime("%a %b %e %H:%M:%S %Y", time.localtime(tv_sec))

Verified during the amail-mci review: the formatted string is byte-identical to `ps -o lstart=` for the same pid, so stored `agents.pid_start` rows need no migration; it works under a profile that denies `/bin/ps` exec, and even under one that denies `kern.proc` sysctl reads.

Scope note: this replaces `pid_start` only. `walk_to_harness` would still need `ps` for `comm`/`ppid` unless `e_ppid`/`p_comm` offsets are also decoded — leave that alone. The InspectionUnavailable plumbing from amail-mci stays regardless, since a non-Darwin host still needs the honest degraded path.
acceptance_criteria: pid_start uses a stdlib ctypes sysctl read on Darwin and falls back to ps elsewhere; reaping and registration work under a sandbox that denies /bin/ps exec; values match ps -o lstart= exactly for existing rows.
close_reason: Subsumed by amail-svb: pid_start now comes from the same sysctl(KERN_PROC_PID) read used for the ancestry walk, verified byte-identical to 'ps -o lstart=' so stored agents.pid_start rows need no migration, with a guarded fallback to ps on an unexpected kinfo_proc size or a non-Darwin kernel.

title: identity's ps subprocess calls crash amail when exec is denied
description:
src/amail/identity.py:30 (pid_start) and :40 (_ps_field) call subprocess.run(["ps", ...]) with no OSError handling. If the sandbox or environment denies exec of ps, Python raises PermissionError/FileNotFoundError and every amail command dies with a traceback — the same failure class as amail-qz5, one layer down.

Reproduced 2026-09-07 under `sandbox-exec` with a profile containing `(deny file-write-mode)`: with the qz5 chmod fix in place, `amail whoami` got past amail_home and then died with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: 'ps'`. (ps is setgid, so that profile blocks its exec; the point is that an unavailable ps must degrade, not crash.)

Both call sites already have a degraded path defined by their return contract: pid_start returns None, _ps_field returns "". They simply do not catch the exec failure.
acceptance_criteria: pid_start and _ps_field return their documented empty value when ps cannot be executed, and amail commands still work (or report a clear one-line error) with ps unavailable. Regression test simulates the exec failure.
notes: Found while verifying amail-qz5. Related to acceptance gate 9 (sandbox/permissions).
close_reason: Fixed: identity.InspectionUnavailable distinguishes 'ps cannot run' from 'pid is gone'; SessionIdentity.pid_start is now optional so a sandboxed session still resolves its own session_key (keeping the inherited-pin conflict check alive); reap returns early rather than marking unverifiable agents offline; register refuses cleanly; detect_branch, doctor and waiter._pid_running (EPERM means alive) hardened; db.connect raises MailboxUnavailable instead of tracebacking. Verified live under sandbox-exec denying /bin/ps: whoami, roster, inbox, doctor all work and nothing is falsely reaped. 8 new tests.

title: A Codex thread registered before its rollout exists becomes a permanently undeliverable mailbox
description:
A Codex session whose process dies before the thread's rollout file is written leaves amail holding a mailbox that can never be delivered to.

Observed 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4). A `codex exec` run was killed mid-flight; its SessionStart hook had already registered `neumann@64` on `codex:01a07d5e-2244-79a0-8f59-cc75d3e961f9`. No `rollout-*-01a07d5e-*.jsonl` was ever written, so:

    $ codex queue --thread 01a07d5e-... --message "test"
    Error: ... no rollout found for thread id 01a07d5e-... (code -32603)

`amail send` reports it honestly — "pushed 0/1 — the rest will see it via a waiter or hook backstop" — but there is no backstop: that thread can never be resumed, so the mail is unreachable forever while the agent still appears in `amail roster --all`.

This is narrow (it needs a session killed inside a short window) and the row is harmless apart from being undeliverable. The question is whether anything should detect it. Options: `amail doctor` could check that a codex-route agent has a rollout; `reap` could mark a codex agent offline-and-unreachable when `codex queue` reports an unknown thread id; or this could simply be documented as a known dead-mailbox case.

Note docs/acceptance-gates.md currently states that "`codex queue` only fails on an unknown thread id, not on a stopped one" — that is still true, and this is precisely how a registered thread id becomes unknown.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and implement one of: doctor detects a codex-route agent with no resumable thread; reap marks such an agent unreachable; or the case is documented as known. Whichever is chosen, a sender is not told mail will arrive via a backstop that cannot exist.
notes: Second instance of the same class, same day: a 'codex resume' that failed during bootstrap ('thread ... already has an active writer', code -32600) had already registered wallace@63 on codex:01a07d5b-4511-7e40-97e5-c1c1cd01b7fc. No rollout file exists for that thread either. So the window is not only a killed 'codex exec' -- any Codex startup whose SessionStart hook fires before the thread is durable can mint an undeliverable mailbox. Both instances are visible in 'amail roster --all' as ordinary offline agents.
close_reason: Fixed at the surface the acceptance criteria named: a sender is no longer told mail will arrive via a backstop that cannot exist. routing.ring now returns PUSHED/FAILED/UNREACHABLE instead of a bool (UNREACHABLE is 'no rollout found for thread id', which is permanent), ring_all returns (pushed, unreachable), and amail send reports an unreachable recipient plainly. The offline warning is a prediction made before the push, so the push result now supersedes it rather than contradicting it in the next line. Verified live: send to the rollout-less thread neumann@64 prints 'cannot be reached now or later'; send to genuinely offline planck@65 still queues and still promises resume delivery. Chose not to have reap mutate such rows -- reaping marks endpoints offline and never destroys mailboxes, and the row is harmless once send tells the truth.

title: db.amail_home chmods on every call, crashing amail under the Codex sandbox
description:
src/amail/db.py:60 runs home.chmod(0o700) on every invocation, even when the directory already exists with the right mode. Under Codex's seatbelt sandbox that raises PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted: '/Users/<user>/.amail', and every amail command dies with a raw Python traceback before doing anything. Observed live 2026-09-07 in a 'codex exec' session (CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt): 'amail whoami' produced a 13-line traceback instead of output.

Two defects in one: the chmod should only run when amail creates the directory, and a permission failure reaching the user as an unhandled traceback is the wrong surface for a tool whose docs promise 'amail doctor' explains degraded modes.
acceptance_criteria: amail commands work under the Codex seatbelt sandbox when ~/.amail already exists with mode 0700. A permission failure that genuinely blocks the mailbox reports a clear one-line error naming the directory, never a traceback. Regression test covers a pre-existing home that cannot be chmodded.
notes: Relevant to acceptance gate 9 (sandbox/permissions), which is still unrun. Found while diagnosing amail-v9s.
close_reason: Fixed: amail_home only chmods a home that is not already 0700, and a permission failure raises db.HomeUnusable which the CLI prints as one line. Verified live under sandbox-exec denying file-write-mode on ~/.amail: 'amail whoami' works. Tests: test_existing_private_home_is_not_chmodded, test_unusable_home_raises_a_clean_error, test_unusable_home_is_one_line_not_a_traceback.

title: amail inside a Codex session adopts the launching Claude session's mailbox
description:
`amail` run as a shell command *inside* a Codex session resolves to the identity of the Claude session that launched Codex, and therefore reads and writes the wrong mailbox.

Observed live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4) during the amail-3rp verification. A Codex thread (franklin@51, `codex:01a07d43-…`) was woken by a queued amail header and correctly tried to act on it. Its `amail read 3` failed with `no message 3 for hilbert@48`, and `amail doctor` inside that session reported:

    identity: claude:58a3f59d-5420-45b9-bc8b-4cf29d5db2b6 (pid 86257)
    agent: hilbert@48

hilbert@48 is the *Claude* session that spawned the Codex process. Mail addressed to franklin@51 is therefore undeliverable in practice even though push, wake, and the receiving-side instructions all work.

Root cause: Codex does not export `CODEX_THREAD_ID` into the environment of the commands it runs, but the inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` / `CLAUDE_PID` from the parent Claude session are still present. `identity.resolve` has no `expect_harness` on a plain CLI call, so `_probe_claude` hits first, returns a real session_key, and `walk_to_harness` — which would have found `codex` in the pid ancestry — is never consulted. The pin-conflict check added in 85ad490 does not fire either, because the resolved identity genuinely matches an existing agent row.

This is the general case of the contract already stated at the top of identity.py: "a Codex process which inherited a Claude session's env must never adopt the parent's mailbox". Today that is only enforced for hooks, which pass `expect_harness`.
acceptance_criteria: A shell command run inside a Codex session resolves to that Codex session's mailbox, not to an inherited Claude identity, with no env scrubbing by the caller. 'amail read <id>' succeeds end to end for mail addressed to that Codex agent. Regression test covers a claude-env-polluted environment whose pid ancestry is codex. Verified live and recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
notes: Found while verifying amail-3rp live. This is the practical blocker behind amail-8ny's 'still untested' authority half and behind amail-up1's symptom; check whether up1 is a duplicate of this. The db.connect and register traceback crashes seen in the same run were fixed under amail-mci.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live. Root cause was probe order plus an untestable tie-break: a Codex session launched from a Claude session's shell has BOTH CLAUDE_* (inherited) and CODEX_THREAD_ID (exported by Codex, contrary to the original bead text), and _probe_claude ran first. Resolution now falls back to the process tree when more than one harness claims the environment, nearest ancestor wins, and ancestry is read with sysctl(KERN_PROC_PID) via ctypes rather than ps -- Codex's own seatbelt denies exec of /bin/ps, which is exactly where the question is asked. Claude is matched by CLAUDE_PID, not by comm (its launcher execs a versioned binary, so comm is e.g. '2.1.263'). kinfo_proc offsets are guarded by a size check and covered by a test against a spawned process. Verified live on codex-cli 0.153.4: 'amail doctor' inside a nested Codex session now reports codex:01a07d5a-... / halley@62 instead of the parent's hilbert@48. Recorded in docs/acceptance-gates.md. Also subsumes amail-lru.

title: A resumed Codex session gets a new thread id and loses its mailbox
description:
'codex resume' gives the session a thread id different from the one SessionStart registered, and no new registration happens on resume. Verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4): thread 01a07cce-... was registered as franklin@39; after resuming, the agents table gained no row for the resumed session, and registry.current_agent for the resumed thread id returns None.

Consequences: a resumed Codex session cannot read its own mail, does not appear in the roster, and cannot be sent to — while the mail addressed to its pre-resume mailbox sits unread in an agent nobody is attached to any more. This also breaks the 'a mailbox outlives its endpoint' contract in the design doc, which assumes re-registering a session_key revives the same agent id; resume changes the key, so revival never fires.
acceptance_criteria: A resumed Codex session resolves to the same mailbox it had before the resume, or amail explains the state and offers a documented way to reattach. Verified live with a dated record in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
notes:
RETESTED 2026-09-07 on codex-cli 0.153.4: the premise does not reproduce for a clean resume. Thread 01a07d43-9090-7ff2-a521-feefa539f348 was created by 'codex exec' and registered as franklin@51. After the process exited and 'codex resume <id>' ran in a pty, the SAME thread id was used: the rollout's resumed turn carries that thread_id, agent 51 went back to status='working' on the same session_key, no second row was created, and its queued mail was drained and announced. Resume preserved both the thread id and the mailbox.

The symptom originally recorded here ('current_agent for the resumed thread returns None') is now believed to have been amail-svb: inside a Codex session, amail resolved to the launching Claude session's identity, so the Codex row looked absent. svb is fixed.

SECOND OBSERVATION, same day, contradicting the first: 'codex resume 01a07d5a-...' registered a NEW agent, wallace@63, on a DIFFERENT session_key codex:01a07d5b-4511-7e40-97e5-c1c1cd01b7fc, created at 19:32:11 — the moment that resume was launched. That resume then failed to bootstrap: 'thread 01a07d5a-... already has an active writer (code -32600)'.

So resume behaviour is NOT uniform. The difference may be that the second resume failed during bootstrap because a writer lock was held by another Codex client on this machine (ChatGPT.app shares the same session store). Retest deliberately before closing: resume a cleanly-exited thread with no competing client, and separately resume a locked one, and record both outcomes.
close_reason:
Not reproducible on codex-cli 0.153.4; closing with evidence. Three clean 'codex resume' runs (threads 01a07d43-9090, 01a07d5f-8e4e, and the 3rp verification) each preserved the thread id, revived the SAME agent row on the same session_key, drained the queued mail and, in the last one, read it end to end. Resume does not mint a new thread id and does not lose the mailbox.

The symptom originally recorded here -- 'current_agent for the resumed thread returns None' -- was amail-svb: inside a Codex session, amail resolved to the launching Claude session's identity, so the Codex row appeared absent. That is fixed and verified.

One residual, filed separately as amail-nxt: a resume that FAILS during bootstrap (writer lock held by another Codex client) registers a throwaway agent on a thread id with no rollout, which is then permanently undeliverable. That is a different defect from the one described here.

title: In-session 'amail read' inside a Codex session resolves to the wrong agent identity
description:
A Codex session that registered correctly as its own agent still resolves to a DIFFERENT agent when it runs 'amail' commands during the session. Verified live 2026-09-07 (codex-cli 0.153.4): thread 01a07cce-6cc0-7541-8022-06e2630c42c2 registered via SessionStart as franklin@39, but when the agent ran 'amail read 2' inside that session it got 'no message 2 for watson@34' — watson@34 being the unrelated Claude session that launched it. The message is addressed to 39, so the read is correctly refused; the identity is what is wrong.

Reproduced three ways, each more isolated than the last, all with the same result: (1) pty child of the Claude Bash tool; (2) same, with AMAIL_AGENT_ID / CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID / CLAUDE_PID popped from the child env before execvp; (3) a detached tmux session launched with those vars scrubbed at both the tmux and codex layers, so the codex process is a child of the tmux server, not of claude. Env scrubbing and reparenting both failed to fix it, so the cause is neither of the two mechanisms install.md's mitigation ('env -u ...') addresses.

Distinct from amail-3um, which fixed the HOOK path by making the hook's harness argument authoritative (d8368ed). A bare 'amail read' passes no harness argument, so identity.resolve falls back to _PROBE_ORDER = (_probe_claude, _probe_codex) and something Claude-shaped still wins inside a Codex session. Root cause not yet identified — do not assume pid ancestry without checking, since reparenting did not help.
acceptance_criteria: A Codex session running 'amail read <id>' resolves as its own registered agent. Root cause identified (not just worked around), regression test added, and re-verified live in a detached Codex session with a dated record in docs/acceptance-gates.md.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-07. Two-part, and my earlier note on this bead was wrong.

CORRECTION: the claim that 'env scrubbing and reparenting both failed to fix it' was not sound. Those runs were confounded — the tmux sessions were blocked on an interactive 'choose working directory' prompt and were only displaying a REPLAYED transcript of the earlier contaminated run, so no fresh read ever ran. Verified afterwards with 'ps eww' on the live codex process (133 env vars readable) that the scrub does take effect: AMAIL_AGENT_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_PID were all absent.

Actual mechanism, reproduced deterministically against the real mailbox with registry.current_agent:
  A registered thread, no pin -> franklin@39      (correct)
  B registered thread, pin=34 -> LookupError conflict (correct, pre-existing)
  C resume-new thread, pin=34 -> watson@34        (THE BUG)
  D resume-new thread, no pin -> None

Part 1: 'codex resume' hands the session a thread id that was never registered, so there is no native row (filed separately). Part 2: with no native row, current_agent accepted AMAIL_AGENT_ID after checking only that the agent EXISTS — never that it belongs to this session. The existing conflict check was guarded by 'native_row is not None', so the pin was trusted in precisely the case where it is least trustworthy. An inherited pin from the launching Claude session names a real agent and won silently.

FIX: identity.SessionIdentity gains a 'native' flag (False when the harness was guessed from pid ancestry — a guess is not grounds to reject a pin). current_agent now rejects a pin whose agent's session_key differs from a natively resolved identity. Verified end-to-end through the installed CLI: the scenario that returned 'no message 2 for watson@34' now exits 1 with 'identity conflict: AMAIL_AGENT_ID=34 is a claude mailbox but this session resolves to codex'. Live Claude session unaffected (still watson@34); 64 tests pass.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed. current_agent accepted an inherited AMAIL_AGENT_ID whenever no native mailbox matched, validating only that the agent existed rather than that it belonged to this session. Fixed in 85ad490 with a regression test; verified end-to-end through the installed CLI. The other half of the root cause (resume loses the mailbox) is filed as amail-up1.
